system.notes:
Public face of the Universal Brotherhood's Seattle chapter. Ostensibly hosts charity coordination, volunteer scheduling, and community events. In practice, the DS contains encrypted membership files, financial laundering records, and communications with non-human entities that have no business corresponding with a human charity.

Notable data: Coded contact lists, financial flows to unknown offshore accounts, encrypted comms referencing "the Feast". DS-A is filled with convincing decoy charity data — the real prize is DS-B, reachable only through the CPU. The IC here is not standard corporate stock; it behaves strangely and does not appear in any publicly available IC database.

nodes.name: System Access Node
nodes.description: Warmly presented public gateway. The Brotherhood's Matrix presence is deliberately inviting — no barriers, soothing aesthetics, helpful prompts asking how to donate or find a local centre. A decker scanning this SAN sees what looks like a low-security charity host with nothing to hide. That appearance is the entire point.

nodes.name: I/O Port — Community Centre Kiosk
nodes.description: Brotherhood community centre kiosk terminals — available in every Brotherhood-run facility across Seattle. They appear to be public access points for booking counselling sessions or checking meal schedules. The jackports behind each kiosk panel connect directly to the host infrastructure. Brotherhood staff are always present and always watching.

nodes.name: Sub-Processing Unit
nodes.description: The routing hub looks exactly like it belongs to a small charitable organisation — modest memory allocation, benign process names, no visible IC listed in the host directory. Deckers who reach this node often conclude they are nearly done. They are not. Something here quietly logs every action.

nodes.name: Data Store — Community Records
nodes.description: Donor records, volunteer rosters, meal programme schedules, community event archives. Beautifully maintained — a completely convincing charitable organisation record system. The data is real. It is also entirely useless paydata. DS-A is a honeypot, filled with information a decker would be satisfied to walk away with. It is not what anyone who matters actually wants from this host.

nodes.name: Slave Node — Membership Registry
nodes.description: The Brotherhood tracks its members in obsessive detail: attendance records, personal disclosures made during counselling sessions (stored without consent or knowledge), psychological profiling, loyalty assessments, and flags for individuals deemed 'ready for deeper involvement.' This node controls access to member facilities. The data here has value — but it is clearly a secondary system, not the heart of the operation.

nodes.name: Central Processing Unit
nodes.description: The Brotherhood's actual administrative core. Security escalates sharply here — the warm, charitable aesthetic of the outer nodes is completely absent. The CPU manages IC deployment, DS-B access keys, and encrypted communications with Brotherhood leadership. There is a second data store reachable only from this node; it does not appear on any host directory visible from the SPU.

nodes.name: Data Store — Operational Archives
nodes.description: Not visible from the SPU. Accessible only through the CPU. The real operational data: safe house coordinates for Brotherhood personnel, indoctrination programme materials and progress reports, contact protocols for Brotherhood cells across the PCC, Aztlan, and CAS, financial routing through shell entities, and encrypted communications that reference things a human charity has no business knowing about. This is what the Johnson is paying for.

ioPorts.name: Brotherhood Community Centre Kiosk
ioPorts.physicalLocation: Available in all Universal Brotherhood community centres across Seattle — Redmond, Puyallup, Tacoma, and several Barrens locations. Kiosk terminals are in the public waiting areas, no credentials required. The jackport is behind the kiosk panel; a flat-head screwdriver or a quiet moment alone with the kiosk is all that is needed. Brotherhood volunteers staff the centres continuously. They are not armed — but they are observant, they report to someone, and they are never alone.

triggerSteps.label: TS 1
triggerSteps.description: ARis activates first, invisible — presenting as an environmental feature of the charitable host interface. It mimics the welcoming aesthetic, feeding the decker misleading routing suggestions. Simultaneously, Looper deploys: the decker's movement commands loop without feedback, making it appear they are navigating nodes when they are not. Without a Detection program, a decker may not realise for several passes that they are going in circles. The Brotherhood sysop is already watching.

triggerSteps.label: TS 2
triggerSteps.description: Scrambler launches — all data the decker reads from this point is subtly corrupted. Names, financial figures, dates, and contact details are transposed or replaced with plausible-looking fabrications. A decker who downloads DS-A data now may walk away confident they have the Brotherhood's records, carrying perfectly crafted disinformation. The Scrambler does not announce itself.

triggerSteps.label: TS 3
triggerSteps.description: Authenticator deploys at the CPU barrier. The Brotherhood's credential system validates against an internal member registry with no public reference database — standard forged SINs will not pass. The authentication challenge presents as a Brotherhood doctrine assessment: a series of ideological questions with no correct answers in any public record. Only genuine insiders can respond correctly. The system has no lockout — it simply reports failure to the sysop and keeps the decker talking.

triggerSteps.label: TS 4
triggerSteps.description: Blaster launches. The Brotherhood's aggressive IC arrives as a complete tonal shock — the warm charitable aesthetic vanishes entirely. Overload attack, Moderate damage, no warning dialogue. A decker who relaxed based on the host's apparent character will be caught entirely off-guard. The transition is deliberate.

triggerSteps.label: TS 5
triggerSteps.description: Gemini deploys — two coordinated instances pursuing the intruder across the host. The Brotherhood's sysops are not corporate professionals: they are true believers who treat Matrix intrusion as a personal violation of their community. The two Gemini instances are logged internally as 'Shepherd' and 'Flock.' They work as one and cover every movement path simultaneously.

triggerSteps.label: TS 6
triggerSteps.description: SN lockdown. All Brotherhood community centre facilities across Seattle simultaneously secure — doors locked, member movement suspended under a pretextual 'safety procedure.' Brotherhood staff are alerted via encrypted channel that an 'external audit' is occurring. Physical security — Brotherhood volunteers and dedicated security personnel, not mercenaries — begin moving to all kiosk jackpoint locations. These people are motivated by belief, not nuyen. That makes them more dangerous.

triggerSteps.label: TS 7
triggerSteps.description: Killer IC deploys from CPU. Physical damage in VR-Hot. DS-B access suspended. The Brotherhood's sysop has escalated to the organisation's internal security council — individuals whose names appear in no public database. Lethal countermeasures are authorised. The Killer here is not a standard IC package; it does not appear in any public IC reference database. Its attack patterns are unusual.

triggerSteps.label: TS 8
triggerSteps.description: DS-B contents receiving an additional encryption layer — keys held off-site with Brotherhood leadership, inaccessible from within the host. A mirror of the most sensitive data is simultaneously transmitted to a secondary location the runners will never find. Whatever they came for is leaving. The Brotherhood does not lose data. It relocates it.

triggerSteps.label: TS 9
triggerSteps.description: Convergence. GOD response. The Brotherhood does not wait — their internal response team was dispatched at TS 6. These are not corporate security contractors; they are individuals who believe the organisation is worth dying for. And killing for. The decker's Matrix signature and any available biometric data have been logged in an internal registry. The Brotherhood has a long memory and no statute of limitations.
